page: Microsoft Azure E2a_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance allocates two dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with multithreading enabled. It features 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage includes 54 GB of local SSD space, while no discrete GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned.

Performance evaluation reflects the single-core strength of the Zen 3 architecture alongside the physical constraints of a single-core dual-thread footprint. The instance delivers steady single-thread performance, recording 1582.0 in the Geekbench single-core benchmark, 26.15 GB/sec in gzip compression, and a PassMark memory score of 2021.37. However, parallel throughput is heavily constrained by having only two execution threads; multi-core Geekbench reaches 1974.0, PassMark CPU totals 3138.26, and Clang compilation scores 1982.0. Memory bandwidth reaches 32.32 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 22.49 GB/sec for writes, while static web serving throughput caps at 2.51 GB/sec.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the E2a_v4 offers an economical entry point for workloads requiring substantial memory allocations without the cost overhead of higher core counts. The primary tradeoff lies in raw compute throughput, where intensive parallel computing, compilation, and high-frequency transaction processing are limited by the single physical core. Consequently, the instance is best suited for small in-memory caches, lightweight database servers, microservices with modest CPU requirements but elevated RAM footprints, and development or staging environments.
description: Microsoft Azure E2a_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring two dedicated vCPUs mapped to one physical AMD EPYC 7763 core running at 3.525 GHz on x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, and 54 GB of local SSD storage, the instance excludes discrete graphics processing. Benchmark results demonstrate capable single-core execution, achieving 1582.0 in Geekbench single-core and 26.15 GB/sec in gzip compression, though multi-threaded output is structurally capped by the dual-thread boundary, as shown by a Geekbench multi-core score of 1974.0 and PassMark CPU score of 3138.26. The configuration offers cost-efficient memory density at low compute scale, making it practical for light database instances, small Redis or Memcached nodes, memory-heavy background tasks, and low-traffic enterprise microservices.
